sources.entry: Python: _A proof-of-concept imitation of Docker, written in 100% Python_

summary.one_liner: mocker is a two-day proof-of-concept imitation of Docker written in pure Python that pulls Docker Hub images and runs them using Linux namespaces, cgroups and network namespaces.
summary.what_it_does: The tool downloads an image's layers from the Docker public registry and extracts them into a local folder, and lists the images already downloaded with their sizes. The "run" command creates a veth bridge in the root namespace, puts the container in its own network namespace with a veth1 adapter at 10.0.0.3/24 and a default route via 10.0.0.1, and creates a cgroup for its processes. It then chroots into the extracted image directory and executes the image's Cmd with its environment variables, writing output to /tmp/stdout. The README says the image is chrooted from the squashed download rather than mounted as a btrfs snapshot, and that NAT networking is unfinished. It is meant to show how container isolation works and how the Docker image format is structured, not to be a usable container runtime.
use_cases: learn how Docker container isolation works
demonstrate namespaces and cgroups in a talk or tutorial
pull Docker Hub images without the Docker daemon
inspect Docker image layers and format
run a simple container from a Docker image on Linux
notable: Implements container isolation in pure Python using kernel namespaces, cgroups and network namespaces
Pulls images from the Docker public registry and extracts their layers locally
Written as an educational companion to a PyCon AU 2017 talk
Lists downloaded images in a table with name, version, size and file
caveats: Linux only; README says it was tested on CentOS 7 and Ubuntu 14
Explicitly a proof of concept written in two days; the author says not to take it seriously
Networking is half-finished with no NAT, and some image start commands fail
